name: Antonio B. Won Pat International Airport
before:
Guam's only international airport, three miles east of Hagåtña, and a hub for United Airlines. It is also the main cargo hub for Asia Pacific Airlines.

There is one quirk that catches people out. Because every flight here needs a customs or immigration check, the concourse was never designed to keep arriving and departing passengers apart. The only ordinary way in is through security and the only ordinary way out is through immigration.

The terminal runs across three levels: arrivals, customs and baggage claim in the basement, ticketing on the apron level and the gates, immigration and offices on the third floor. It opened in two phases in 1996 and 1998 as part of a 741 million dollar programme.

The frontage carries stylised latte stone motifs, the latte stone being an icon of modern Chamoru identity.

There are two runways, of 12,014 and 10,014 feet, on the site of the former Naval Air Station Agana.
after:
Guam's only international airport, three miles east of Hagåtña, and a hub for United Airlines. It is also the base of the cargo carrier Asia Pacific Airlines.

Because every flight here needs a customs or immigration check, the concourse was built to be shared by arriving and departing passengers. Since January 2022, the airport says, a third-floor International Arrivals Corridor has taken arriving passengers from the gates straight to the US Customs and Border Protection hall, kept apart from departing passengers.

The current terminal opened in two phases, in 1996 and 1998.

There are two runways, of about 12,000 and 10,000 feet, on the site of the former Naval Air Station Agana.

claims.claim: since January 2022 the International Arrivals Corridor has kept arriving passengers apart from departing ones
claims.inAfter: Since January 2022, the airport says, a third-floor International Arrivals Corridor has taken arriving passengers from the gates straight to the US Customs and Border Protection hall, kept apart from departing passengers.
claims.note: The old text's quirk was out of date. The operator says it completed the International Arrivals Corridor in January 2022 (in use from 25 January, first flight Jin Air from Incheon; Phase I, for gates 4 to 10, in February 2021): a sterile third-floor corridor from the gates to the US Customs and Border Protection hall, 'completely separated from departing passengers'. Attributed to the airport because the completion rests on its own pages; Wikipedia describes the same corridor and its purpose, but only as a project. Wikipedia and the operator also disagree on its cost (110 against 137 million dollars), so no cost is given. Review (24 Sep): 'apart from departing passengers' became 'kept apart from departing passengers', as 'apart from' could be read as 'except'.
